newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New firms fight for HK telephone market share.
newsitem.headline: New firms fight for HK telephone market share.

text.p: Two of Hong Kong's new telecom service providers on Thursday stepped up the war for market share, launching new international calling products.

Wharf (Holdings) Ltd's New T & T Hong Kong Ltd launched a new promotion, and New World Development Ltd's New World Telephone has teamed up with Dah Sing Bank to offer a New World Telephone MasterCard (NWT MasterCard).

Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd has a theoretical monopoly on international calls which expires in 2006, but faces stiff competition from new entrants who are able to resell existing international lines or who run call back services.

New T&T's new promotion, "Talk Longer, Pay Less", covered the United States, Canada, Australia, Britain, China, Japan and Singapore, New T&T said in four time bands with call rates getting cheaper the longer they are.
For example, callers to the United States pay HK$2.84 a minute for up to seven minutes, but a half hour calls would cost HK$1.69 a minute.
New World Telephone and Dah Sing Bank, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Dah Sing Financial Holdings Ltd, said their NWT MasterCard combined credit card services and calling card benefits, they said.
The cards offered 60 free international call minutes a year, they said.
